', '[Fuente: Manual 8 | Página: X | Sección: 6| Título: X] LASERON El PLC activa está marca para indicar que el láser está encendido. response: To configure the laser PWM on the A218 with the 8070 CNC, follow these steps: 1. Determine the frequency and duty cycle of the PWM you want to use. 2. Set the PWMFREQ register with the desired frequency (between 2 and 5000 Hz). 3. Configure the PWMDUTY register with the desired duty cycle (between 1 and 1000). 4. Parameterize the NLOCOUT parameter with a value of 8 to use the local outputs associated with the LI/O1 and LI/O2 pins for the PWM. 5. Activate the PWM from the PLC using the PWMON flag. 6. To cancel the PWM after executing M30 or reset, set the PWMCANCEL parameter to "Yes".  This will configure the PWM of the laser on the A218 with the 8070 CNC.

', '[Fuente: Manual 7 | Página: X | Sección: 12| Título: X] Por defecto, el CNC calcula el espacio y el avance sobre los tres ejes principales, y el resto de ejes les siguen al avance que les corresponda. De esta manera, en una máquina con cinemática y RTCP activo, en la que se mueven más de tres ejes, la punta de la herramienta se mueve al avance programado. Sin embargo, cuando en estos mecanizados hay discontinuidades de movimiento en los ejes no principales, este proceso puede generar irregularidades en el perfil de velocidad y por lo tanto el movimiento resultante puede no ser siempre continuo. The door micro detects the pressure on the operation console buttons and generates a digital signal accordingly. 2. The digital signal is sent to the PLC through a connection cable. 3. The PLC processes the signal and assigns it to the corresponding variable (V.G.KEY). 4. The PLC checks the V.G.KEY variable to verify if a key has been pressed. 5. If a key has been pressed, the PLC activates the M101 flag and writes the key code to the G.KEY variable. 6. The PLC uses the G.KEY variable to simulate the keyboard and send the key press and release codes to the CNC. 7. The CNC processes the codes and performs the corresponding action, such as activating a movement. 8. The CNC activates the M101 mark when the operation begins and maintains it until it ends. 9. response: Normal stop is used to stop the machine in normal situations, such as when an inspection or maintenance needs to be carried out. The emergency stop is used in emergency cases, such as if there is a danger of injury to people or damage to the machine.  The emergency stop should be used only in emergency cases, since it leads to the disconnection of the different systems and motors of the machine. In normal situations, the machine should not be switched off using the emergency stop button.  Normal stop can be performed using the normal stop button or the stop button on the operation console. The emergency stop can be carried out using the emergency stop button in the electrical cabinet or the button panel of the machine.  Data can be backed up using backup, which can be performed when there is no power (for example, emergency button pressed). This allows you to restore the CNC configuration (OEM and user data) later if necessary. To diagnose the fault, the following steps can be followed: 1. Verify that the power supply is correctly connected and that the mains voltage is adequate. 2. Check the tightness of the power bus plates and the power supply fuse. 3. Check the correct condition of the lines and verify that the application does not require strong current peaks and that the mains power line has an acceptable impedance. 4. Verify that the crowbar connection (internal or external) is correct and that the internal crowbar/soft-start resistance is in perfect condition and is well connected. 5. If the power supply is a PS-25x, check the status of the Ballast resistor. 6. For any power supply, verify that excessive time has not been spent loading the DC BUS of a compact regulator. 7. If the problem persists, contact Fagor Automation for more information and help.  If errors are detected in the controller software, the error log can be reviewed to obtain more information about the problem and its possible cause.

response: If the master spindle is not selected and a spindle speed command is sent, the CNC will select a master spindle according to the criteria explained in the 8070 CNC programming manual. If the channel has several spindles, the CNC will choose the master spindle according to the criteria described above, such as the first spindle configured according to the machine parameters or the original spindle if any of the spindles is the original master and is not parked. If none of the above rules can be applied, the following criteria will be followed: if any of the heads is the original master, it is assumed to be the master head. If it is parked, the next head from the original configuration is chosen and so on. If no heads of the original configuration are available on the channel, the first head of its current configuration is assumed as master. If it is parked, the next head is chosen and so on.
